verdict.label: HOLD — Iran Strikes Muddy Oil-Relief Thesis; NVDA Execution Triggered
verdict.rationale_short: The May 25 night BUY call was directionally correct at the index level — NVDA opened $220.90 above the $212 conditional entry threshold and ES futures implied SPX opening above 7,460. But US military self-defense strikes in southern Iran overnight sent Brent crude +3.4% to $99.39 and drew Iranian retaliation threats, contaminating the clean oil-bearish thesis the BUY depended on. WTI at $92.85 is $3.75 below Friday's close, but the Brent/WTI spread widening to $6.54 is the Hormuz disruption signature. Hold established positions; no new broad-index additions until Iran clarity; April PCE Thursday is a live binary.

bear_case: The Brent/WTI spread widening to $6.54 ($99.39 vs. $92.85) is the Hormuz disruption signature — Brent prices direct Middle East supply interruption risk while WTI tracks domestic US supply. US military strikes in southern Iran drew Iranian retaliation threats; if Iran's foreign ministry formally declares the ceasefire void and signals imminent Hormuz access disruption, Brent accelerates toward $105-108 and WTI reverses from $92.85 toward $97-100, eliminating the 30Y yield relief window before it completes even one confirmation session. April PCE on Thursday at a prior 2.40% YoY with inflation spreading across food, airfares, and AI chips leaves no margin for an Iran-driven oil reversal. If SPX closes below 7,440 with Brent above $103 on any session before PCE Thursday, HOLD upgrades immediately to Step Aside.
